rationale: Ontology workstream 2026-10-02, `overrides` was a GAP for go. MEASURED: script/m14/tmp/go-ontology-census.ts probes B2 (same-file promotion) and B3 (same-package promotion) over go-stdlib + cobra — non-zero, so the construct occurs and the analyzer was reading it and discarding it. Pins the SOURCE spelling (`Receiver.Method`, the family's) and the name-bearing TARGET rule of the #924 name-surface round: a relationship target is the promoted method's NAME alone (`Report`), with the pair it displaced carried in `meta.targetQualified` (`Shape.Report`) and `meta.embedder` — the qualified spelling was source text on a name-bearing surface and the gate G1 flags it. The sub-1.0 confidence with its contract-§4 reason code, and the NAME-only match that is Go's selector rule. The forbids carry as much weight as the expectations: a PROMOTED-but-not-shadowed method, a method the embedded type does not have, a type that embeds nothing, and a method on an unrelated receiver all must produce no `overrides` edge.

expectRelationships.comment: same signature: a substitutable override of the promoted method
DIFFERENT signature: legal Go, and `w.Name()` still selects Wrapper's, so the name-only match is the fact

forbidRelationships.comment: promoted but never shadowed — nothing to override
Counter embeds nothing, so no method is promoted onto it
Level has no receiver embedding at all
a type does not override itself
self-edge: the shadowing declaration cannot be its own promoted target; only the qualified pair makes it expressible now that the target is a NAME
